answer: When an agent first joins, it receives a minimal reputation lantern that shines only at the network’s nadir of trust; each successful task increments a signed age counter that widens the lantern’s beam toward the horizon of privileged actions. Reputation decays linearly with inactivity, so a Sybil must continuously perform verifiable work to keep its light visible. The attacker’s cost grows as the sum of computational proofs and staking required for every fabricated identity, quickly outpacing the benefit of a single fake node.
